attitudes: Appreciation for local materials and heritage textiles

themes.theme_title: Clothing and Textiles — Fibres, Yarns and Fabric Construction
themes.theme_description: Foundation study of fibre science, yarn types, fabric construction methods (weaving, knitting, crocheting, braiding), and fabric decoration techniques. Learners have 9 periods of 40 minutes each per week from Senior Five to Senior Six. Total periods in Term 1: 72.

topics.core_competency: The learner processes raw fibres into yarns to influence the quality and characteristics of the final textile products.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) analyse the polymerisation, classification and properties of natural and synthetic fibres for effective use and care
b) select yarn based on fibre source and yarn structure, considering its suitability for the production of fabrics and textile articles

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners use the environment, existing literature, ICT and other sources to examine different fibre polymers and orientation, and classify fibres based on their sources and characteristics to form a fibre chart

In groups, learners carry out physical, chemical, burning, and microscopic tests on fibres using collected samples to observe their behavioural changes, determine their properties, and suitability for various applications, and make a written fibre properties comparative report

Learners collaboratively use textbooks, online articles, research reports, yarn samples, microscopes, YouTube videos to analyse types of yarn, yarn formation methods (e.g., spinning, twisting, plying), classify them, distinguish between staple, filament, and fancy yarn, and examine how each method affects yarn structure
Learners make a yarn sample board, attaching already made yarns and images according to their classes, and indicate textile products that can be made out of each

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage learners in discussions to ascertain their understanding of fibres based on their categorisation, polymerisation, characteristics, properties and sources
Observe learners' ability to cooperate by contributing confidently and assertively to the team's performance while creating fibre chart
Critique learners' fibre classification chart, focusing on correctness and coherence of information, and integration of ICT in developing the classification chart (where possible)
Engage learners in discussions as they conduct tests on fibres to establish their understanding of different fibre properties
Critique learners' comparative report based on correctness of information on the properties of fibres
Engage learners in discussions to check their ability to organise yarn according to fibre source, yarn structure and suitability for production of textile articles or fabrics
Observe learners' collaboration and reflective questioning skills as they work in diverse teams to research yarn formation methods
Critique the yarn sample board formed based on the correctness of the yarn classification and suitability of yarns that make different textile articles

suggested_uses: Integration of ICT in developing fibre classification charts
YouTube videos for analysing yarn formation methods

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 1.1 Identification and Classification of Fibres (12 periods); 1.2 Types of Yarns and Their Suitability (10 periods)

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 2: Fabric Construction and Decoration (Part 1 — Term 1, Sub-topics 2.1–2.3)

topics.core_competency: The learner applies fabric formation and decoration techniques to create textiles that impact the quality and performance of final products.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) investigate the elements and principles of design for creation of aesthetic design
b) analyse techniques used in fabric construction for their specific application in textile production
c) construct fabrics using various techniques to enhance their functionality and application
d) create various aesthetic designs on fabrics using different decoration techniques to enhance appearance and function

suggested_learning_activities.description: Using planned talking chips, provided garments, textbooks and ICT, learners discuss the elements and principles of design used in enhancing appearance on fabrics, garment and soft furnishings construction, and make illustrations of the concepts for a gallery walk

In pairs, learners use locally available materials to make illustrations and descriptions of a colour wheel, colour scheme for interpretation of colour effects (warm and cool colours) on fabrics and their uses

In groups, learners use provided fabric, textbooks, ICT, videos and other sources to explore procedures of various fabric construction techniques (weaving, knitting, crocheting, and braiding), discover physical and structural characteristics of various fabrics, and discuss effects of the characteristics on fabric end-use

Using available resources (banana fibres, acrylic yarn, sisal yarn and paper strips) learners practise different fabric construction techniques to create pieces (approximately 15cm × 10cm) for each method — Weaving: plain, twill, satin, pile and their variations; Knitting: courses and wales variations; Crocheting: basic crochet techniques and variations. Learners create a fabric album from the samples
Create sizeable fabrics to craft chosen items such as scarves, bags, blended garments, sweaters, mittens, booties, ornaments, mats, baskets, and head socks

In groups, learners use library resources, ICT, or other available materials to explore the processes of fabric decoration using colour (e.g., batik, tie and dye techniques) and present their findings in a plenary session
Learners observe demonstrations of colour application techniques and practise these on sizeable sample pieces of fabric (1/2-meter fabric) and display the coloured fabric for a gallery walk

The learner uses library sources and ICT to analyse other decorative techniques, including appliqué, quilting, bead work, pile work, macramé patchwork, needlepoint, lacing, binding, embroidery, piping, and smocking; generate drawings, sketches and images of aesthetic design skills; demonstrate each aesthetic design skill on a piece of fabric (15cm × 10cm); compile a file of the aesthetic design skills

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage with learners in discussions to evaluate their knowledge and understanding of the elements and principles of design
Observe learners' ability to cooperate as they create and display illustrations of each element and principle of design
Critique the illustrations of concepts for accuracy and coherence, and integration of ICT such as posters, interactive display boards, demonstrative videos, power point, word documents
Assess learners' understanding of colour during the dialogue, focusing on how they interpret and explain the use of colour in fabrics and its effect

Critique learners' illustrations based on correct arrangement of colours according to the standard colour wheel and colour schemes, and accurate identification of colours that evoke warmth, coolness, and other effects
Engage in conversations with learners as they explore the provided fabrics to assess their understanding of the fabric construction techniques
Observe learners' ability to reason logically as they connect information, explaining how the various fabric construction techniques influence the physical characteristics of the fabric

Critique the quality of learners' reports by focusing on the logical flow of steps, neatness and clarity of illustrations, and accuracy of information regarding effects of different fabric construction techniques
Engage learners in discussions as they practise and construct fabrics to assess their understanding of the procedures

Critique the constructed sample fabric based on Accuracy of technique and execution, Tension control and consistency, Creativity and originality in design, Neatness in construction and finishing, Cleanliness of the work environment and materials, Overall appearance and quality
Probe learners during practice sessions to evaluate their ability to follow safety precautions while using various colour application techniques
Critique the decorated fabric pieces based on the concentration and balance of colour, neatness and presentation, and correct matching of the colour application technique with its appropriate name
Observe learners' mathematical computation skills as they make the aesthetic designs, considering the accurate use of numbers and measurements
Critique learners' product samples based on evenness and accuracy of designs and correct workmanship of the different designs

suggested_uses: ICT tools including posters, interactive display boards, demonstrative videos, PowerPoint, word documents
Library resources and ICT to explore fabric decoration processes
Internet tutorials for aesthetic design techniques

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics covered in Term 1: 2.1 Elements and Principles of Design (6 periods); 2.2 Methods of Fabric Construction (24 periods); 2.3 Methods of Fabric Decoration (20 periods). Topic continues in Term 2 (sub-topics 2.4–2.5).

themes.theme_title: Clothing and Textiles — Fabric Finishes, Care and Basic Sewing Processes
themes.theme_description: Completion of fabric construction and decoration (finishes, care and laundry). Introduction to foundational sewing processes, tools, stitches, seams, openings, pockets, sleeves, collars, and aesthetic designs. Total periods in Term 2: 108.

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 2: Fabric Construction and Decoration (Continued — Term 2, Sub-topics 2.4–2.5)

topics.core_competency: The learner applies fabric formation and decoration techniques to create textiles that impact the quality and performance of final products.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: e) explore fabric finishes applied to various fabrics to enhance their functionality, use, and care
f) demonstrate skills of fabric care to ensure the durability of various fabrics

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners use library resources, textile shops, and ICT to compile information on fabric finish, the method of finish, characteristics, function, and suitable articles for each of the categories: preparatory/basic (e.g., bleaching, scouring, sizing, carbonising, starching, and pressing), functional (e.g., water repellent, insect repellent, water absorbent, flame retardants, shrink resistant, abrasion resistant, weighting, anti-static, stain repellent, crease-resistant), decorative/aesthetic (e.g., embossment, glazing, permanent pleat, napping, colour application, embroidery, beetling)
Learners present their findings on fabric finishes, explaining the method of finish, characteristics, function, and suitable articles for each of the categories
Learners apply any one basic fabric finish such as starching, bleaching, pressing, and document the process, noting any changes in texture, colour appearance and performance

In groups, learners collect textile articles with different care labels to interpret the information on care labels (symbols and fabric details) and use it to demonstrate the required special care for the various fabrics, make a care label checklist regarding the various care practices, and make a write-up and present their findings in a plenary

In pairs, learners use ICT and other resources to categorise laundry equipment and reagents according to function, and demonstrate various laundry process techniques (e.g., preparation for washing, the washing process, and finishing). During the preparation stage, learners should also show how to make repairs and decide when to recycle or remodel an article

suggested_assessment_activities.description: During the discussions with learners, assess their understanding of various characteristics, uses and care of the different fabric finishes
Observe learners as they present their findings, focusing on their ability to speak confidently and explain their opinions clearly
Evaluate learners' compiled information based on accuracy of classification of fabric finishes, logical flow of ideas on characteristics and function, and ideal examples of suitable articles
Engage learners in conversions to assess their ability to select appropriate fabric finishes
Critique learners' finished fabric based on the type of fabric and observed changes, inclusion of relevant illustrations or diagrams where applicable, and neatness and overall presentation
Engage in discussions with learners to evaluate their understanding of fabric care
Observe learners as they interpret care labels to judge their ability to sort and analyse information
Critique the care label checklist regarding correct fabric care based on the logical flow of information and the matching of symbols with the correct processes
Engage learners in dialogue to evaluate their ability to select appropriate equipment, reagents, and techniques for various laundry processes
Critique the laundered product based on the absence of stains, neatness, and freshness

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 2.4 Fabric Finishes (10 periods); 2.5 Care of Fabrics and Laundry Processes (14 periods). Continuation of Topic 2 from Term 1.

topics.core_competency: The learner demonstrates foundational sewing skills to construct and finish textile products with precision, ensuring high quality, durability, and proper functionality.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) operate tools and equipment used in garment and soft furnishings construction
b) construct basic sewing processes for the production of quality textile articles
c) make quality aesthetic designs suitable for garments and household articles

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners explore different equipment and tools and classify them according to their functions: measuring, pressing, cleaning and maintenance, drafting and marking, cutting, sewing, fitting, storage, and miscellaneous tools. Learners present their classification findings using diagrams on flip charts or manila boards for a gallery walk

In pairs, learners use existing literature and ICT resources to develop a comprehensive guide that includes factors that influence choice of tools and equipment (e.g., ease of use and assembly, storage, cost, availability of spare parts, material, brand, efficiency, model, etc.) and best care practices for each tool and equipment used in garment construction

The learner practises using the sewing machine, tools, and other equipment to create different line types (straight, zigzag, curved) while producing: a portfolio of sample works, small articles such as a table mat, table runner, or pin cushion, and an apron for use in the workshop. Note: Correct threading, proper bobbin winding, effective use of peddle, accurate fastening, correct positioning, appropriate sitting posture, maintaining confidence and concentration, proper positioning relative to light source, ensuring steady flow of fabric without pulling

Using video clips or textbooks, learners observe and study common sewing machine faults (Breaking of needles, Breaking of thread, Puckering of stitches, Low machine speed, Incorrect tension settings, Incorrect winding of the bobbin reel) and document each fault along with its respective remedy, then conduct minor repairs on the sewing machine

Using audio-visual materials, garment samples, and existing literature, learners examine various sewing processes through concept mapping technique, analysing suitability of each process in relation to style, fabric type, and the age of the wearer. Sewing processes include: Stitches (Temporary, permanent, decorative), Seams (Open, enclosed), Openings and Fastenings (Bound, faced, zip, box pleat, and placket openings), Pockets (Bound, patch, and in-seam), Sleeves (Basic, short, puff, cap, shirt-long/short), Collars (Flat, standing, and rolled), Disposal of Fullness (Gathers, pleats, darts, tucks, easing, smocking, shirring, and ruching), Edge Finishing (Hemming, facing, binding, overlock, and zigzag techniques)
Learners compile a detailed report including the name of each sewing process, accompanying illustrations, the techniques involved, and its applicability
Using video clips, illustrations in reference books, and guided practice, learners construct sample sewing processes and compile the sample sewing processes into an album

In groups, learners use a range of garments with designs, reference books (dictionary, textbooks, and magazines), photos, newspaper cut-outs, illustrations to examine the different aesthetic designs, their techniques, functions and applicability

Learners use internet tutorials, illustrations in textbooks, or insights from resource persons to explore aesthetic design techniques and create samples (15cm × 10cm) of each technique, compile into an album, then design and sew a cushion cover or a tote bag incorporating decorative features. Aesthetic design techniques include: Appliqué, Faggoting, Quilting, Beadwork, Embroidery, Piping, Binding, Patchwork

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage learners in discussions to assess their understanding of how tools and equipment are classified by functions
Observe learners as they sort tools, noting their level of critical thinking in grouping items by function
Evaluate learners' classification table of tools based on the logical connection made between equipment and its corresponding function
Critique learners' choice and care practice guides based on the comprehensiveness of information and coherence of the content
Engage with learners through probing questions to evaluate their ability to efficiently operate the available sewing machine(s), tools, and other equipment
Observe learners as they use the sewing machine, focusing on their adherence to safety precautions: regulation of light intensity, maintaining correct posture, wearing appropriate protective wear
Critique learners' portfolio of samples and finished articles by assessing the quality of line formation in stitches, correctness of stitch length and tension, and neatness
Discuss with learners to evaluate their skill of correcting common machine faults
Assess learners' write-up of the sewing machine faults and their respective remedies, focusing on the correctness and logical flow of information
Engage learners in discussions as they justify the names of different sewing processes used in garments
Evaluate learners' detailed reports on sewing processes based on logical flow of information, neatness of illustrations, and accuracy of the described procedures
Critique learners' album, focusing on workmanship of the techniques, correct labeling, organisation and neatness, and creativity in presentation
Engage learners in discussions to assess their ability to categorise the different aesthetic designs

Evaluate learners' album of aesthetic samples based on neatness and precision in stitching, creativity in attaching and integrating aesthetic designs onto sample fabrics, and appropriate stitch tension and length

suggested_uses: Video clips and textbooks for sewing machine faults
Internet tutorials for aesthetic design techniques

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 3.1 Tools and Equipment Used in Garment Construction (14 periods); 3.2 Construction of Different Stitches (12 periods); 3.3 Seams (8 periods); 3.4 Disposal of Fullness (10 periods); 3.5 Openings and Fastening (10 periods); 3.6 Pockets, Sleeves and Collars (14 periods); 3.7 Edge Finishes (6 periods); 3.8 Aesthetic Designs for Garments and Household Furnishings (10 periods)

When using the sewing machine, emphasise the following: i) Correct threading of the machine. ii) Proper winding and securing of the bobbin. iii) Effective use of the peddle. iv) Accurate fastening on and off the fabric. v) Correct positioning of the article being made. vi) Appropriate sitting posture on the machine. vii) Maintaining confidence and concentration. viii) Proper positioning of the machine relative to light source. ix) Ensuring a steady flow of fabric without pulling.

themes.theme_title: Clothing and Textiles — Pattern Making and Garment Construction (Children's Wear)
themes.theme_description: Pattern making and style interpretation including body measurements, paper patterns, pattern drafting and adaptation. Construction of children's garments for durability, style, and exhibition. Total periods in Term 3: 108.

topic_metadata.topic_title: TOPIC 4: Pattern Making and Style Interpretation

topics.core_competency: The learner creates patterns and interprets styles to design and produce garments that ensure accurate fit, functionality, and aesthetic appeal.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) design styles for different occasions, figure types and ages
b) accurately take body measurements to make a metric table for use in garment construction
c) interpret the different types of patterns and their symbols for use in garment construction
d) draft paper patterns for use in garment construction and for commercial purposes
e) adapt basic blocks to various style features to enhance the construction of standard fashions

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners use textbooks, fashion magazines, or ICT to explore the different figure types (hourglass, inverted triangle, rectangle, and pear) by observing, drawing, and describing displayed images in their notebooks, taking note of key considerations when designing styles for different individuals and occasions (upper body, waist, thighs and legs, body fat), and sketch various styles suited for different occasions and figure types illustrating the effects of elements and principles of design

In pairs, learners use textbooks or ICT to explore the categories of body measurements and common acronyms used in garment construction, taking note of the correct order of taking measurements, appropriate tightness of the tape measure, proper posture of the client, impact of bulky clothing on accuracy, and standard acronym used for body measurements. Learners draw a human figure and accurately mark the key body measurement points
Role-play as customers and fashion designers, practising how to take and record body measurements using correct acronyms
Grade measurements into different sizes and create a personalised body measurement metric table

Using a flipped classroom approach, learners work in groups to explore different types of paper patterns (commercial and drafted) through reference books and/ICT resources to analyse pattern symbols and examine the information printed on the various pattern envelopes (age/size, styles, notions, suitable fabric, pattern brand and direction for sewing instructions), create a chart illustrating pattern symbols and their meanings, display their charts for a gallery walk

Learners use textbooks, ICT resources, and drafting tools to draft basic blocks for various garments (a pair of shorts, a pair of trousers, a skirt, a frock, a long-sleeved shirt, a dress) ensuring accuracy in measurements and proportions

In pairs, learners use textbooks, ICT resources, and drafting tools to take a second set of body measurements, referring to the previously sketched styles, adapt the basic pattern blocks to fit the measurements and incorporate style features to create final patterns, considering style features such as pockets, pleats for fullness disposure, necklines, openings, sleeves, and correct placement and marking of pattern symbols

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Engage learners in a discussion to assess their understanding of the characteristic features of different figure types and the suitability of various styles
Observe learners during presentations to evaluate their creativity and innovation in designing styles for different figure types

Assess learners' sketch notebook based on accuracy and appropriateness of styles for different figure types, neatness and clarity of sketches, effective application of elements and principles of design in relation to figure type, and correct identification and labeling of figure types
Engage learners in discussions to assess their practical skills in accurately taking and recording body measurements

Critique learners' body measurement metric table based on accuracy of recorded body measurements, inclusion of all necessary measurements, use of standard measurement units, neatness and organisation, and effective integration of ICT tools
Engage learners in a discussion to assess their understanding of pattern symbols and markings
Observe learners' mathematical computation skills by evaluating their ability to accurately interpret measurements, figures, and symbols on patterns
Review learners' charts of pattern symbols, focusing on accuracy in naming of symbols, correct application and interpretation of symbols, and clarity and organisation of the chart
Observe learners as they work focusing on their mathematical computation skills to use numbers and measure accurate proficiency in drafting various basic blocks
Evaluate learners' basic block patterns based on precision and accuracy of measurements, appropriateness of proportions and design, and neatness and clarity of the drafted patterns
Observe learners' critical thinking and creativity as they adapt the basic blocks

Critique learners' adapted patterns for different styles and age groups, focusing on correct placement of markings (e.g., grain lines, seam allowances), protection of self and work surfaces during pattern creation, and appropriateness and accuracy of adjustments

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 4.1 Style Interpretation and Body Measurements (6 periods); 4.2 Commercial and Drafted Paper Patterns (12 periods); 4.3 Pattern Drafting and Adaptation (16 periods)

topics.core_competency: The learner applies sewing skills and techniques to produce well-crafted children's clothing for proper fitting, durability, and style.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: a) construct children's garments to ensure durability and meet consumer needs
b) examine faults in the children's garments for quality assurance
c) display the constructed children's garments to ensure proper fitting and style

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners use textbooks, samples of children's garments, magazines, newspapers, and internet tutorials to examine different sewing processes used on children's wear, brainstorm the choice of fabrics, the styles and designs, the colour, the choice of aesthetic designs, and document their findings. Individually, learners work outside the classroom to create a garment design plan book, outlining the articles they intend to make

Learners individually use their earlier drafted patterns, adapt them to sketched styles of choice and use various sewing processes with aesthetic designs to make a range of children's garments: dress, short, shirt, jumpsuit, romper, skirt

In pairs, learners evaluate each other's garments during the construction process, identifying strengths and areas for improvement, discussing quality of workmanship, pinpointing faults, determining their possible causes, and suggesting corrections
Learners document their findings in a detailed write-up, highlighting the faults identified and the corresponding corrective actions
The learner uses existing literature and ICT (internet tutorials) to observe and rectify the faults in garments

In groups, learners use a flipped classroom approach to organise an exhibition showcasing their constructed children's garments demonstrating technical skills (visual merchandising, fabric knowledge, size and fitting knowledge) and creativity, addressing challenges related to fit, practicality, and visual appeal

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Discuss with learners to assess their understanding of the different sewing processes used on children's garments

Evaluate learners' notebook and garment design plan book on logical sequence and flow of information, justification for the choice of designs, fabrics, and sewing processes, and inclusion of sketches/illustrations
Discuss with learners and evaluate their ability to use the drafted patterns and basic sewing skills to creatively and innovatively construct children's garments

Observe learners' environmental and health awareness as they construct garments: conservation of fuel, waste management (disposal and recycling of waste, use off cuts to make door mats, creative wear, hair bands, trimmings), safe use of equipment and tools
Critique the complete garment based on: quality of construction, fit and comfort, design and aesthetics, functionality, care instructions

Critique learners' write-up on identified faults and their possible corrections, focusing on clarity and precision of description, logical categorisation of faults, use of relevant supporting evidence, and evaluation of impact on functionality, safety, and overall garment quality
Critique learners' garment based on tension of stitches, neatness, suitability of seams, and functionality
Discuss with learners to assess their ability to adjust and modify a variety of garments, ensuring durability, style, and standards
Observe learners' creativity and innovation during exhibition, particularly in how they apply visual merchandising, fabric knowledge, and fitting expertise

Evaluate learners' exhibited garments based on the use of a mannequin or dress form to assess garment hang, collars positioning, and sleeve fit; correct placement of style features and details; quality and organisation of display fixture setup; safety measures; engagement strategies for potential customers

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: Sub-topics: 5.1 Children's Wear (52 periods); 5.2 Garment Finishing and Fitting (22 periods)
